video_title: Stellar Hits $4B+ in RWA's: Why Wall Street Institutions Are Choosing Stellar | Denelle Dixon
gist: Stellar Development Foundation CEO Denelle Dixon discusses Stellar passing about $4B in tokenized RWAs, the US Bank stablecoin pilot, MoneyGram's Colombia card, DTCC's H1 2027 timeline, and why institutions pick open networks with built-in compliance and privacy controls.

insights.claim: Stellar's tokenized real-world assets reached roughly $4B, about 360% annual growth per the host, which CEO Denelle Dixon attributes to partners onboarded last year now distributing their assets this year.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Institutional pipeline on Stellar converts to on-chain balances with roughly a year's lag; more issuers are 'in the queue'.
insights.quote: so much of the number that you're we're talking about in terms of crossing the 4 billion mark has to do with the work we did last year.

insights.claim: Franklin Templeton issued the first money market fund on Stellar (process started 2019, issued around 2021), and its Benji asset has many different retail and institutional holders rather than a few institutions.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Holder breadth suggests real distribution rather than a single-counterparty balance.

insights.claim: Stellar's RWA mix spans private credit, money market funds and other asset types, and Dixon dismisses the issuer concentration worry (Speiko is about $1.55B of the ~$4B per the host) as evidence of product-market fit.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Concentration in one winning issuer is read by the network as validation; a bear would see single-issuer dependency.
insights.quote: I'm not worried about concentration at all.

insights.claim: Dixon says holders buy tokenized money market funds for yield rather than because they are digital assets, and that issuers sometimes cannibalize their existing users rather than gaining net new ones.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Tokenization alone does not create new demand; distribution is the bottleneck for issuers.
insights.quote: it's a money market fund that that drives yield

insights.claim: The host cites a stat that less than 10% of tokenized assets are actively used in DeFi; Stellar's answer is 'RWA-Fi', blending issuer controls (freeze, clawback) with DeFi use as collateral, lending and borrowing.
insights.speaker: Host (The Defiant) and Denelle Dixon
insights.so_what: The next RWA leg depends on composability with DeFi while preserving issuer compliance controls.

insights.claim: Redstone provides 24-hour price data for RWAs on Stellar, filling a missing link because RWAs lack round-the-clock price discovery, which enables their use in DeFi.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Off-hours RWA pricing is a gating item for collateral use; oracle providers are beneficiaries.
insights.quote: you don't always have the 24-hour price analysis

insights.claim: US Bank, which Dixon calls a top-five US institution, completed a Stellar stablecoin pilot (announced November last year) running the full lifecycle: mint, cross-border send from the US to a European treasury, payment, redemption, clawback and freeze.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: A top-five US bank testing issuer controls end to end within about 9 months signals bank stablecoin issuance moving beyond talk, relevant to bank consortium efforts.
insights.quote: They went through the whole life cycle to make sure that it all worked.

insights.claim: US Bank's pilot proceeded under the existing GENIUS Act framework without waiting for the CLARITY Act, per Dixon.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Bank stablecoin activity does not require further market-structure legislation, lowering regulatory-delay risk.
insights.quote: you have the genius act that allows them to do this kind of thing

insights.claim: MoneyGram, a 75-year-old firm operating in about 200 countries, is working with Rain and Stellar on a stablecoin debit card starting in Colombia, with expected expansion beyond Colombia.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Remittance incumbents are using stablecoin rails for last-mile retail use, a read-through for cross-border payment fees.

insights.claim: Dixon frames Stellar's traction as a barbell: retail reach via MoneyGram's Colombia card on one side and institutional treasury use via US Bank on the other, both on one network.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Pitch is that one network can serve both ends, a differentiator versus chains focused on one.

insights.claim: Stellar had around 40 asset-backed 'stablecoins' (including peso-backed) about eight years ago, most no longer around because they were too early and lacked product-market fit until much later.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Stellar claims early-mover design for stablecoins but earlier cohorts failed on demand timing, not technology.

insights.claim: DTCC chose Stellar as a partner (announced in May), went to testnet in July with parts of the system, and has told Stellar to expect the first half of 2027, which Dixon says remains on track.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: DTCC on Stellar is guided for H1 2027, not this year; Dixon did not confirm the host's November date.
insights.quote: it's going to be the first half of 2027 and we are still on track for that

insights.claim: Dixon claims Stellar has 99.99% uptime over 10 years, with a single outage of about 42 minutes in 2019 in its 14-year history, and says uptime plus configurable compliance controls (authorization-required, clawback, freeze) are key institutional requirements.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Uptime record and composable controls are Stellar's institutional selling points.
insights.quote: Stellar has a 99.99% uptime just in the last 10 years.

insights.claim: Dixon claims Stellar has the most native building blocks for privacy of any open public chain, with composable choices such as privacy pools, private tokens or blurred transaction recipients, and says every institution asks about privacy.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Privacy is a coming institutional requirement; chains with native optional privacy may gain issuer share.
insights.quote: Institutional privacy becomes like this piece that every institution asks about.

insights.claim: Dixon argues open public versus permissioned chains is 'not even a question anymore' for institutions, since legacy closed software has gone stale and global integration requires a shared open network like the internet.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Narrative is shifting toward public chains for institutional settlement; permissioned-chain vendors face pressure.
insights.quote: I don't even think it's a question anymore.

insights.claim: Stellar has no validator incentives, so institutions that have issued assets join the Tier 1 validator set (added in threes) purely to govern the network and secure features like issuer-enforced finality.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Issuer-driven governance aligns the network with issuer needs but offers no staking-yield narrative.

insights.claim: Dixon says crypto is in a bear market while adoption of the tech stack is booming, comparing it to the dot-com retraction that kept serious builders, and says questions about whether the tech will survive are settled.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Institutional building continues independent of prices, a divergence between sentiment and adoption.
insights.quote: in a retraction in terms of like the crypto market and the bear market

insights.claim: Dixon expects natively issued on-chain equities (a couple of companies have done it already) and more cross-border payments to come to Stellar.
insights.speaker: Denelle Dixon (CEO, Stellar Development Foundation)
insights.so_what: Next product frontiers named are native equity issuance and cross-border payments.
